seo.title: Karpacz live cameras — the Karpatka ski slope in real time
seo.intro: Our live cameras in Karpacz show the Karpatka ski slope at ul. Myśliwska 3, right below Śnieżka in the Karkonosze Mountains. Before you leave home, check the snow cover, how the run is groomed and how busy the lifts are — live.
seo.viewsText: Camera 1 covers the top lift station and camera 2 the bottom station. Camera 3 shows the beginner conveyor lift and the bar in winter, and the view of Sokoliki and Krzyżna Góra in summer. Together they show the whole slope — from the bottom of the lift to the top of the run.

slope.title: Ski slope in Karpacz
slope.text: Karpatka is a ski slope in Karpacz with two T-bar lifts, a conveyor lift for beginners and free parking right next to the run. A good place both for first runs and for polishing your technique at an easy pace.

school.title: Ski lessons — ski school on the slope
school.text: There is a ski and snowboard school right on the slope. Instructors teach skiing and snowboarding (55-minute lessons) for kids and adults — one-to-one or in groups. You can rent all the equipment on site.

sledding.title: Sledding hill
sledding.text: Next to the ski runs there is a snow-groomed sledding hill, with sleds included in the ticket. The cameras make it easy to check whether conditions are good for sledding with the kids.

rentalPrice.q: How much does it cost to rent skis or a snowboard in Karpacz?
rentalPrice.a: A full set of equipment (skis or snowboard, boots and poles) at the Karpatka rental shop costs {day} per day and {night} for night skiing (17:00–21:00).

passPrice.q: How much is a ski lift pass in Karpacz?
passPrice.a: Prices start at {hourNormal} per hour ({hourReduced} reduced). A day pass (9:00–16:30) costs {dailyNormal} ({dailyReduced} reduced), and an evening pass (16:30–21:00) — {eveningNormal} ({eveningReduced} reduced). See the full price list in the Prices section.

ownGear.q: Do I need my own ski equipment?
ownGear.a: No. The rental shop is on site and provides full equipment — skis, snowboards, boots and poles — no preparation needed.

learnBasics.q: Can I learn to ski from scratch in Karpacz?
learnBasics.a: Yes. Beginners have a gentle conveyor lift and ski and snowboard instructors offering private and group lessons (55 minutes, from {lessonSolo} for 1 person, +{extra} for each additional person).

smallKids.q: Is there anything for young children who don't ski yet?
smallKids.a: Yes — the sledding hill (1h for {sled1h}, 2h for {sled2h}) and a conveyor lift for the little ones that makes the first attempts at skiing easier.

sleddingWhere.q: Where can I go sledding in Karpacz?
sleddingWhere.a: The Karpatka slope has a prepared sledding hill — we provide the equipment (sleds), a safe environment, artificial snow and lighting.

sledsIncluded.q: Are sleds included in the sledding hill ticket?
sledsIncluded.a: Yes — sleds are included in the sledding hill ticket, so there's no need to bring your own.

sleddingSnow.q: Is the sledding hill covered with artificial snow?
sleddingSnow.a: Yes, it is covered with artificial snow, so it can be used even when there is little natural snow.

sleddingTicket.q: Where can I buy a sledding hill ticket?
sleddingTicket.a: You can buy a sledding hill ticket on site at the Karpatka ticket office.

location.q: Where exactly is the Karpatka ski lift?
location.a: The Karpatka ski lifts are at ul. Myśliwska 3 in Karpacz (58-540), in the Karkonosze Mountains, right below Śnieżka, with free parking right next to the slope.

openingHours.q: What are the current opening hours of the slope and the rental shop?
openingHours.a: Opening hours depend on snow and weather conditions, so we update them regularly — check the conditions board at the top of the page and the footer.

schoolPage.title: Ski school in Karpacz — ski lessons and ski kindergarten
schoolPage.description: Ski school in Karpacz, Poland: ski kindergarten for children from 3–4 years, ski and snowboard lessons for children and adults, a beginner conveyor lift and ski rental on site.
schoolPage.subtitle: Ski and snowboard school for children and adults — right below Śnieżka.
schoolPage.lead: Karpatka instructors teach skiing and snowboarding from the very first step. Lessons take place on a gentle slope with a beginner conveyor lift, and you can rent equipment on site — arrive, sign up and start the same day.

kids.title: Ski lessons for children
kids.text: Children start on the gentle part of the slope with the conveyor lift — away from faster skiers on the T-bar lifts. The instructor works at the child's pace: first getting used to the skis, riding the conveyor and snowplough braking, then the first turns and runs on their own. 55-minute lessons suit the youngest well, and the sledding hill and bar are right next door.

preschool.title: Ski kindergarten in Karpacz
preschool.text: The Karpatka ski kindergarten takes children from the age of 3–4, depending on each child's readiness. Lessons are in groups and run as play, so children learn to ski almost without noticing it is a lesson. They start on the conveyor lift and, once ready, move on to the T-bar lift.

slope.title: A slope made for beginners
slope.text: The Karpatka slope has a gentle, even gradient that is ideal for learning. The conveyor lift lets you start safely without a ski lift, and once you feel confident, the T-bar is the next step — all on one slope, with no transfers and no stress.

adults.title: Ski lessons for adults
adults.text: First time on skis or back on the slope after years? In a private lesson the instructor focuses on you alone: your stance, safe braking and turning — and once you feel confident, you move from the conveyor to the T-bar lift together. Skiers who already ski on their own can polish their technique and carving.

snowboard.title: Snowboard lessons
snowboard.text: Karpatka school also teaches snowboarding. We start with balance and side-slipping on gentle terrain, then turns and riding the lift. You can rent a board and snowboard boots on site.

lessons.title: What are the lessons like?
lessons.text: A lesson lasts 55 minutes — private or in a group with family or friends, and each additional person is just +{extra}. For your first lesson you only need warm, waterproof clothing, gloves and goggles or sunglasses. Skis or a board, boots and poles can be rented by the slope; the full set costs {day} per day.

schoolPage.pricesNote: A lesson with an instructor lasts 55 minutes.

preschool.q: Is there a ski kindergarten in Karpacz?
preschool.a: Yes — the Karpatka slope runs a ski kindergarten for children from 3–4 years, depending on the child's readiness. Lessons are in groups and run as play: first on the conveyor lift, later on the T-bar lift.

age.q: From what age can a child learn to ski?
age.a: Usually from 3–4 years — it depends on the child's readiness. The youngest start in the ski kindergarten on the conveyor lift, and older children can also choose private lessons with an instructor.

price.q: How much do ski lessons in Karpacz cost?
price.a: A lesson with an instructor lasts 55 minutes and costs {solo} for 1 person, {duo} for 2 people, {trio} for 3 people and {quad} for 4 people. Each additional person in the group is +{extra}.

kids.q: Do you offer ski lessons for children?
kids.a: Yes. Children learn with an instructor on the gentle part of the slope with the beginner conveyor lift — on their own or together with siblings or friends.

gear.q: Do I need my own equipment for a lesson?
gear.a: No. You can rent skis or a snowboard, boots and poles on site — the full set costs {day} per day.

snowboard.q: Does the school also teach snowboarding?
snowboard.a: Yes — the instructors teach both skiing and snowboarding, for children and adults.

where.q: Where do the lessons take place?
where.a: At the Karpatka slope, ul. Myśliwska 3 in Karpacz, right below Śnieżka. There is free parking by the slope.

book.q: How do I book a lesson?
book.a: Call {tel} — we will agree on the time and number of people. At weekends and during school holidays it is worth booking in advance.

rentalPage.title: Ski rental in Karpacz — skis and snowboards at the Karpatka slope
rentalPage.description: Ski and snowboard rental in Karpacz, Poland, right at the Karpatka slope. Full set (skis or board, boots, poles) {day} per day, {night} for evening skiing. Ski school on site, free parking.
rentalPage.subtitle: Skis, snowboards, boots and poles — right at the slope, no need to bring your own.
rentalPage.lead: No need to pack skis in the car. The rental shop is right at the Karpatka slope: we will fit you with skis or a board, boots and poles, and a few minutes later you can head to the lift or your first lesson.

gear.title: What can you rent?
gear.text: Ski set: carving skis, boots and poles. Snowboard set: board and boots. Helmets are also available on site — we especially recommend them for children and beginners.

fit.title: Equipment that fits you
fit.text: We match skis and boots to your height, weight and skiing level — differently for beginners and for confident skiers. That makes the first runs easier and safer.

evening.title: Evening skiing
evening.text: You can also rent equipment for evening skiing. An evening set (17:00–21:00) costs {night}, and the evening lift pass is valid from 16:30 to 21:00.

school.title: Rental and ski school in one place
school.text: First time on skis? Combine equipment rental with a lesson at the Karpatka ski school — the instructor will check that everything fits and take you straight to the beginner conveyor lift.

price.q: How much does ski rental in Karpacz cost?
price.a: A ski set (skis, boots, poles) costs {day} per day and {night} for evening skiing (17:00–21:00).

included.q: What is included in the set?
included.a: The set includes skis or a snowboard, boots and poles. You can also rent a helmet on site.

snowboard.a: Yes — a snowboard set costs the same as a ski set: {day} per day and {night} in the evening.

where.a: At the Karpatka slope, ul. Myśliwska 3 in Karpacz, right below Śnieżka. You can leave your car in the free car park by the slope.

hours.q: What are the rental opening hours?
hours.a: The rental is open during the slope opening hours, which depend on snow conditions. You will find the current hours in the page footer and the slope conditions on the live webcams.
